reviewer: outdoor_pool assistant subagent; contributor to greenery/population implementation, separate direct final-image inspection, not blinded external validation.
review_method: Opened all five current PNGs directly with view_image after the final rerun including the current traffic-hold code and pool-shortcut camera UI branch. No image/runtime edits or engine execution during review. Current PNG hashes below identify the exact reviewed images.
comparison_to_prior_visual_assessment: Same acceptance and limitations as the earlier five-image review. Tree/people coverage remains visible, and sparse sectors 4/6 remain explicitly unaddressed visual-density limitations.

traffic_revision_present.meaning: The rerun includes current traffic code. Five still images independently review trees, people and cameras; they do not establish traffic braking, release/hold or FIFO behaviour.

images.name: coverage_sector_0
observed: Several original-style articulated people are visible on the foreground public paths, with a continuous row of mapped trees beyond the stone wall.
The original player is fully visible in a normal third-person frame; the present Lotte/high-rise exterior is also visible.
limitations: The broad open foreground remains deliberately sparse. A single still does not establish moving-car behaviour.

images.name: coverage_sector_2
observed: Dense visible tree rows, thin trunks, tree grates and clearance under the crowns create a legible planted street/plaza edge.
The full player and other people are visible near the path and lawn.
limitations: The large lawn is still simple flat game terrain, not surveyed terrain.

images.name: coverage_sector_4
observed: The player and dispersed walkers are visible without geometry hiding the central avatar.
Facade and path edges are legible.
limitations: This broad grey area remains visually empty with very little planting in this view. It is an accepted remaining density/detail limitation.

images.name: coverage_sector_6
observed: The original player and two nearby people remain visible on supported outdoor ground.
Nearby building scale and the entry indication remain readable.
limitations: The large grass surface still feels empty; the source footway is not visually distinct from the grass surface here. This does not establish a finished paved pedestrian street.

images.name: coverage_sector_8
observed: Tree rows, open space below crowns, grates, path surface and the church facade make the street more recognisable.
The player remains fully visible with other people in the courtyard/street setting.
limitations: Close source walls fill portions of the left and right frame edges. They do not hide the central avatar or route but make this particular composition less open.

remaining_limits: Sectors4/6 remain broad, flat and sparsely detailed; 6 lacks a visually distinct footpath surface.
Native crowns and humans retain simple low-poly forms, rather than surveyed species/visitor density or photoreal assets.
Selected view fixtures and twenty-second controller observations do not establish every street view, long-duration performance, whole-city crowd realism, or a human keyboard journey.
Traffic correctness is supported by its separate controller tests, not claimed from these five stills.
final_rerun_context: Current final reports and images include the final pool-shortcut camera UI branch. All current captures were reopened directly after that rerun; the previous acceptance and recorded limitations remain unchanged.
